messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: lavaan 0.5-19 released on CRAN
parts:
Dear lavaan users,

I am happy to announce that lavaan 0.5-19 has been released on CRAN.

This version finalizes the changes (regarding the way general linear
equality constraints are handled) as described in this document. Please,
read it again: http://lavaan.ugent.be/notes/lavaan_eq_constraints.pdf

Other user-visible changes:

- the parameter estimates section of the summary() output has been
redesigned: it now repeats the section headers ('Est' 'Std.Err' etc),
and the number of digits after the decimal point can be changed, as in
summary(fit, nd = 5)

- the modindices() function now only shows modification indices for
'new' parameters (that are currently fixed to zero in the current
model); it does not give you information about what may happen if you
release (general) equality constraints; for that, we need the
lavTestScore() function

- new function lavTestScore() gives univariate/multivariate score tests
(aka Lagrange Multiplier tests) for releasing (typically equality)
constraints in the model

- lavPredict() now consistently ignores the structural component (ie all
regressions); its main purpose is to compute the values for latent
variables; if used with the type = "ov" argument, it will attempt to
compute the values of the indicators of these latent variables; if all
variables in a model are observed, it simply returns the observed
variables; in other words, despite its name, this function does not
'predict' new values for dependent variables, given values of
independent variables, as is common in regression models

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: lavaan 0.5-19 released on CRAN
parts:
On 10/08/2015 03:58 PM, Edward Rigdon wrote:
> I use Rstudio as my R development environment. I've been asking
> Rstudio about updates for R packages, and it still is not offering me
> the lavaan update.

Could it be that you are using OS X Snow Leopard? I noticed that (for
some unknown reason), the binaries for this OS X flavor have not yet
been created on CRAN:

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/lavaan/

But since lavaan does not contain any code that needs to be compiled,
you should be able to install it from source like this:

install.packages("lavaan", repos="http://cran.r-project.org", type =
"source")

Yves.
